intro_script: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from October 26, 2026. We cover 17 top stories, including the robotaxi race in Europe, Toyota's humanoid factory push, and new funding for personal vertical flight.
outro_script: And that's all the circuits for today, October 26th, 2026. From autonomous rides to the European robotaxi battle, keep those algorithms running smoothly. Thanks for plugging into the future with me. See you next time!

items.title: Interview with Arthur D. Little consultant: Europe emerging as battleground for global robotaxi race
items.summary: Europe is emerging as a crucial battleground for the global robotaxi race due to its relative openness compared to the US and China. This fragmentation creates opportunities for robotaxi companies seeking an early market foothold by allowing direct competition between Chinese and Western firms. Success in Europe will depend on vehicle economics, fleet utilization, regulation, consumer trust, and the ability to operate profitably at scale. Markets like Spain and the UK offer distinct opportunities based on regulatory timing and market size. Ultimately, fleet operators who can optimize vehicle utilization and costs are expected to be the long-term winners.

This development signals that regulatory environments and operational efficiency will determine market success for autonomous ride-sharing services.

items.title: Toyota humanoid strategy targets factories in robotics push
items.summary: Toyota plans to invest $6.4 billion annually in factory automation, deploying 400,000 robots to commercialize robotics research. The humanoid strategy focuses on automating factory work and addressing labor shortages rather than pursuing an external robot business first. Toyota's internally developed Eley humanoid learns tasks by observing factory workers using an in-house foundation model. The company emphasizes integrating robots, AI, and production processes into a unified operating system as a competitive advantage. Deployment priority is set for internal factories, with projections estimating Toyota could capture a small segment of the humanoid market by 2035.

This development signals a focus on practical industrial application for advanced humanoid robotics within manufacturing sectors.

items.title: eVTOL company Skyfly lands $10 million to bring personal vertical flight to market
items.summary: Skyfly Technologies secured a $10 million seed round led by HICO Investment Group and Archangel to advance its electric aircraft. The funding will be used to complete the certification of the Axe, a two-seat eVTOL aircraft, and expand production. The Axe is designed to meet updated FAA Light Sport Aircraft rules, offering a cost-effective and aerodynamically efficient design. Skyfly is also developing the Longbow, a hybrid-electric unmanned aircraft for defense and logistics applications. The company's prototype has flown extensively and has a strong pipeline of potential customers.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "eVTOL company Skyfly lands $10 million to bring personal vertical flight to market". The funding was led by HICO Investment Group and Archangel and is allocated to complete the certification process for the Axe, a two-seat electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, and to expand production capabilities. The Axe design adheres to updated FAA Light Sport Aircraft rules, emphasizing an aerodynamically efficient and cost-effective structure. Furthermore, the company is concurrently developing the Longbow, a hybrid-electric unmanned aircraft intended for defense and logistics sectors, building upon extensive prototype flight testing and a defined customer pipeline. This development indicates continued progression in the commercial viability of personal air mobility technologies.

items.title: Schaeffler opens lighthouse factory in Taicang where ‘humanoids will make humanoids’
items.summary: Schaeffler opened a state-of-the-art lighthouse factory in Taicang, China, dedicated to humanoid robotics. This facility features an intelligent assembly line and a training center to facilitate the mass production of humanoid robot components. The factory demonstrates a closed manufacturing loop where humanoids assemble key joint modules for other humanoids. It combines manufacturing expertise with physical AI and digital twins for testing and optimizing production. This initiative aims to drive the adoption of humanoids in industry by accelerating the development of the humanoid robotics ecosystem.

This initiative seeks to accelerate the adoption of humanoids in industry by advancing the entire humanoid robotics development sphere. This development signals a significant step toward industrializing humanoid robotics through advanced manufacturing integration.

items.summary: Industrial robot installations grew to over five million globally in 2026, with China leading in installations. Research is advancing anthropomorphic robotic hands capable of self-supported locomotion and manipulation through reinforcement learning. Investigations in India reveal women are paid to record household tasks to train robots on real-world manipulation. Discussions are ongoing regarding the regulation and potential prohibition of autonomous weapons systems. Studies suggest that perceived fairness, both distributive and informational, can improve acceptance of security robots.

items.title: Teradyne Robotics partners with Sereact to scale physical AI in retail and logistics
items.summary: Teradyne Robotics partnered with Sereact to advance physical AI solutions for retail and logistics. Sereact's Cortex platform runs Universal Robots robot arms to automate unstructured tasks like handling returns and picking. This combined technology handles mixed goods and varied packaging, allowing a single "brain" to manage various tasks across robots. The joint solution is already deployed in Zalando's fulfillment centers in Europe for processing returned fashion items. The collaboration aims to scale these AI-powered automation solutions across various industries globally.

Sereact's Cortex platform utilizes Universal Robots robot arms to automate unstructured tasks such as handling returns and picking within fulfillment operations. The combined technology enables a single intelligent system to manage diverse tasks involving mixed goods and varied packaging across multiple robotic units. This integrated solution is currently operational in Zalando's fulfillment centers across Europe for the processing of returned fashion items. The joint effort seeks to expand these AI-powered automation methods across numerous global industries. This development signifies a tangible step toward deploying complex physical AI systems in real-world commercial environments. Future developments will focus on the global scalability of this integrated automation technology.

items.title: advasolutions automates logistics center of drugstore chain Hebe in Poland
items.summary: advasolutions is implementing a tote-based storage system for the Polish drugstore chain Hebe. This project involves retrofitting an existing building with 66 autonomous advaShuttles to store approximately 20,000 totes at ten meters high. The implementation will occur in phases during ongoing operations, with a go-live scheduled for early 2028, integrated with SAP EWM. The system features automated replenishment and incorporates conveyor technology for discrepancy handling. This solution demonstrates how modular automation can be integrated into live operational environments without major structural changes.

The implementation proceeds in phases during ongoing operations with a planned go-live in early 2028, integrating the system with SAP EWM and incorporating automated replenishment and conveyor technology for discrepancy handling. The project signals continued progression in applying modular automation solutions across complex retail logistics.

items.title: AgiBot Expedition A3 sets dance record with 110 humanoid robots
items.summary: AgiBot Expedition A3 humanoids achieved a Guinness World Record for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously with 110 machines in Jinan, China, on October 24, 2026. The robots coordinated their routines using AgiBot’s LinkBots cluster control and ultra wideband positioning technology, achieving centimeter-level accuracy. The performance included complex maneuvers such as repositioning, jumps, and flips. The record demonstrates fleet coordination rather than industrial productivity, highlighting the challenge of maintaining synchronized motion among numerous mobile machines. Future applications for these robots will focus on cultural performances, public services, and education.

items.title: ETH Zurich team demonstrates Unitree G1 climbing and crawling
items.summary: An ETH Zurich team developed a single policy enabling a Unitree G1 to walk, climb, and crawl without manually scripting transitions between these movements. They trained the system by using 13.2 minutes of human motion data to learn contact patterns. Reinforcement learning in simulation was then used to allow the robot to adapt to new terrains. During operation, onboard sensing and a goal guide the robot's movements without requiring a reference motion for transitions. The team demonstrated climbing, including a ladder recovery, using the learned policy rather than explicitly programmed sequences.

items.title: beRobox unveils advanced palletizer featuring ‘3D dynamic safety’
items.summary: beRobox introduced the "3D Dynamic Safety" module for PALTZ robotic palletizers, creating a dynamic safety zone that moves with the robot. This system uses Sonair's safety-certified ADAR One 3D ultrasonic sensor to provide real-time, three-dimensional detection of people and objects. This allows the safety system to adapt to the dynamic palletizing workspace, enabling safe operator access during operations. The technology allows for more selective reactions to operator interactions without stopping the entire cell. Furthermore, the system maintains presence detection around the robot, preventing unintended restarts when an area is occupied.

items.title: The Air Behind the Robot: Why Compressed Air Piping Decides How Well an Automated Line Runs
items.summary: Compressed air dictates the performance of automated lines because the quality and pressure of the supply directly affect the operation of pneumatic components. Inadequate air delivery causes cycle times to stretch and parts to slip, often leading to maintenance issues that are hard to trace. Leaks, corrosion from moisture, and material choices in the piping network significantly impact long-term operational reliability. Effective distribution requires careful leak detection and material selection to minimize production losses. Modern designs favor flexible loop systems and quick-connect fittings to accommodate plant changes while maintaining system integrity.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "The Air Behind the Robot: Why Compressed Air Piping Decides How Well an Automated Line Runs" reports on how the quality and pressure of compressed air supply directly affect the operation of pneumatic components in automated lines. Inadequate air delivery results in extended cycle times and part slippage, frequently causing maintenance difficulties that are difficult to isolate. The research details that leaks, corrosion resulting from moisture, and the material selections within the piping network significantly influence the long-term reliability of the system. Effective air distribution necessitates meticulous leak detection and careful material selection to mitigate production losses. Modern design approaches incorporate flexible loop systems and quick-connect fittings to allow for plant modifications while preserving system integrity. This emphasis on infrastructure quality is crucial for the continued reliable deployment of advanced automation technologies.

items.title: Welcome, TRON 2!
items.summary: TRON 2 is a modular embodied robot from LimX Dynamics designed for research and prototyping, offering configurable forms like dual arm, bipedal, or wheeled legs. It measures 132 cm, weighs 35 kg, and has a maximum speed of 18 km/h, supporting features such as obstacle avoidance, stair walking, and goods sorting. The robot's skill score is 4/10, indicating it is currently stronger in mobility than manipulation. Developed with a Linux-based system supporting ROS and features for VR teleoperation, it is available for USD 37,700.

items.title: Welcome, StarBot Astra!
items.summary: StarBot Astra is a 152 cm tall, 34 kg humanoid research platform designed for embodied robotics investigation in supervised settings. It features 23 degrees of freedom, electric joints, and hands with five fingers, running a Linux and ROS software environment on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin system. The platform supports research in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, which serve as focused experimental areas. Its low Humanoid Guide score and preliminary ratings indicate it is a preliminary research system, not a mature general-purpose worker. Astra is available for preorder at a starting price of $9,999 for academic and research institutions.

items.title: Hairy Armor For Combat Robot? It’s Not Terrible!
items.summary: An individual wondered if a mane of bristles could serve as lightweight, impact-resistant armor for a combat robot. This experiment was conducted on a robot competing in a plastic antweight division, where the concept seemed promising. The robot's hairy design withstood impacts that broke the outer shells of previous robots. This suggests the idea may have merit for combat robotics designs. Furthermore, 3D printing facilitates the experimentation with unorthodox robot designs.

items.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
items.summary: RepresentNav is a navigation foundation model that constructs a self-constructed representation space from vision foundation models. It uses Representation Residuals, a transformer, to aggregate features from multiple vision models to understand navigation needs. The model also generates "dreams" through a latent chain-of-thought to predict scene representations for future moments. This dream generation is trained jointly with the navigation policy via a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). RepresentNav achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks and improves physical robot performance amid clutter.

items.title: KiRoSe: Using Kinematic Data for Efficient Segmentation of Robot Demonstrations
items.summary: KiRoSe is a framework that utilizes robot kinematic data for efficiently segmenting robot demonstrations. It proposes Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete vocabulary to compactly represent recurring kinematic events, inspired by entropy coding. SMTs are learned by encoding trajectories with temporal supervision and quantizing features. Evaluation shows KiRoSe significantly outperforms baseline methods in F1 quality segmentation. Furthermore, the method can track task progress and detect action reversals on unseen robots.

items.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: SEVI is a framework designed for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world reinforcement learning to address unsafe interactions. It introduces an Evidential Safety Critic that estimates future constraint-violation risk and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. During online learning, SEVI checks actions before execution and overrides them with an offline-trained recovery policy if risk is too high. The method was evaluated on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, demonstrating superior safety prediction and reduced unsafe events compared to other methods. SEVI successfully reduces unsafe events by 13.4 to 57.1 percent while maintaining low-latency execution.

items.title: WorldMirror: Agentic Real-to-Sim Generation of Interactive Worlds from In-the-Wild Robot Demonstrations
items.summary: WorldMirror is an agentic framework that generates interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations. It treats real-to-sim construction as iteratively refining an executable world program through agent planning and tool orchestration. The system utilizes a camera-pose-anchored scene representation to organize spatial context, geometry, and interactive assets. An agent refines reconstructions by diagnosing and correcting errors to ensure physically consistent interactions and trajectory replay. Experiments show that WorldMirror can create visually faithful and geometrically consistent interactive worlds while maintaining the physical validity of recorded robot trajectories.

items.title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
items.summary: FORCA is a coding agent designed for contact-rich robot manipulation that translates visual observations and force/torque measurements into Python programs. It inspects force records and visual outcomes between executions to diagnose failures and revise control logic. The agent achieves this without requiring demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Tested across five real-robot tasks, FORCA improves manipulation accuracy and adapts to changes in object properties. Compared to a vision-only agent, FORCA enhances grasp accuracy and reduces contact loss during tasks like wiping and peeling.

items.title: EgoForesight: Effectively Scaling Policy Learning with Noisy Egocentric Actions
items.summary: EgoForesight is a vision-language-action framework designed to scale policy learning despite noisy egocentric actions. It learns jointly from robot demonstrations and egocentric videos by mitigating the influence of unreliable action labels. The method employs a joint vision-action flow and reliability-conditioned corruption to manage noisy supervision. Furthermore, it utilizes privileged-future representation distillation from demonstrated outcomes to provide complementary supervision. This approach results in steeper scaling slopes, improving performance in real-world and simulated dexterous manipulation tasks.

items.title: Multimodal MPC via Bayesian Set Optimization for Dynamic Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects
items.summary: The paper introduces BM2PC, a Bayesian Multimodal MPC framework for the agile manipulation of deformable linear objects (DLOs). It formulates multimodal planning as a set optimization problem to balance control quality and behavioral diversity. BM2PC efficiently updates multiple promising control modes with low computational overhead through an incremental approach. The framework incorporates an execution dynamics model to compensate for real-world execution mismatches during manipulation. Experiments show BM2PC achieves accurate long-horizon tracking and efficient obstacle avoidance in simulation and hardware.
